topic: Main rotor movements, dy-symmetry of lift feathering, flapping, dragging, hook's joint effect, flapping to equality, phase lag and advance angle concepts
syllabus_extract: Main rotor movements, dy-symmetry of lift feathering, flapping, dragging, hook’s joint effect, flapping to equality, phase lag and advance angle concepts
specific_objectives: 13.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the helicopter control, main rotor movements, translation flight, power, auto rotation, vibration checks and various adjustments.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of Rotor Dynamics Diagrams; Safety: Do not touch rotating models; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation
intro_questions: What are the primary movements of the main rotor?
Define the term 'flapping' in rotor dynamics.
Why is phase lag critical in helicopter flight?

development.content:
Main rotor movements types
Flapping and dragging mechanics
Hook's joint effect explanation
Flapping to equality principle
Phase lag and advance angle

Dynamic symmetry of lift
Feathering control inputs
Translation flight dynamics
Power management basics
Auto rotation entry

Vibration check procedures
Adjustment mechanisms
Ground effect circulation
Recirculation effects analysis
Vertical descent techniques

summary_questions: Explain how phase lag affects rotor blade position relative to the hub.
Describe the relationship between flapping and dragging in forward flight.
How does dynamic symmetry of lift prevent excessive vibration?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the transition from ground effect to free air hover, referencing concepts from the next lesson plan (LP 06).

pft_rows.syllabus: Hovering and forward flight, take off and climb to free air hover, vertical decent ground effect ground cushion re circulation effects, forces in balance during hover, forward flight and transition phenomenon of flap back, factors effecting maximum speed.
